correctness.rationale: For each labeling, let t be the number of 2s. Cases t=0, t=1, and t=2 with same row/same column/opposite positions force, respectively, mn, m+n, n+2, m+2, and 6 weight. At t>=3 weight>=6 and equality forces three 2s, positive support with no isolates, and for m,n>=4 the only feasible three-cell support is a 2x2 L. All equality patterns are explicitly constructed and their disjoint counts summed. Narrow m<=3 cannot achieve weight 6 as an optimum. Graph distances are independently BFS-checked in verify.py on 13 boards with 4,516,156 candidate assignments; tests are finite corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Statement-level published-finding corpus and earlier published-claim comparisons, direct full HTML review of original 2023 HTR article, reading the full closest complete-prism Roman {3} result, and comparison with 2026 2-hop product literature found no same-definition all-minimizer rook classification. value.rationale: A natural invariant introduced in 2023 is solved on a universal two-parameter Cartesian-product graph family. The result is structurally stronger than a scalar minimum: every optimum is classified, the special widths m=2,3,4 are explained, and a rectangle-bijection gives exactly 6 binomial(m,2) binomial(n,2) optimal labelings for m,n>=5. Exact multiplicity of optimizers is a meaningful counting problem for comparing robustness, symmetry, and nearby graph-product families; the family is not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.
